label: Gearbox vehicle speed
notes: 3-wire 12V OEM Toyota E154F VSS; actual road speed not traction control. RESOLVED 2026-09-28 (Daniel) - PCLink DI 8 pull-up ON. Toyota EWD (ST205 service hints, V1 vehicle speed sensor): 4-ground approx 12 V ignition ON (supply), 1-ground 4 pulses per rotor-shaft rotation (output), 2-ground always continuity; EWD glossary: the speed sensor opens and closes a switch, i.e. a switched pulse output read by the ECM SPD and cruise ECU. G4X sources (no G4+): PCLink G4X Help 'Digital Input Wiring' (read at http://www.frozen-cherry.info/Help_File_ENG/digital_input_wiring.htm) - 'If a switch or controller drives low then the Digital Inputs Pull-up Resister will need to be enabled' and 'Some sensors will require that the Digital Inputs Pull-up Resister is enabled'; PCLink G4X Help 'Digital Inputs' - switch on 1.8 V, switch off 1 V. Pull-up ON also reads a driven 12 V output. Calibrate 4 pulses per sensor-shaft turn. Sensor fitted = Toyota 83181-20040 (Daniel 2026-09-28; 1991-97 Land Cruiser FZJ80 / Previa speedometer sensor, 3 blade pins). Mate = Toyota 90980-11143 oval 3-pin socket plug, Sumitomo TS 090 sockets: pin 1 IG +12V switched, pin 2 ground, pin 3 SP1 speed output (Daniel 2026-09-28: draw as-is on the best reading; Toyota 3-wire speed-sensor pinout per the wilbo666 wiki; the EWD V1 pin numbers 4/1/2 are the meter-side connector)

label: EPS relay battery feed
notes: From high-current fuse block HCFB H4 (ST185-CabinPower, glove box). Sized 2026-09-28: Bussmann AMI-60 (60 A) at HCFB H4 and 8 AWG feed. Pump draw: about 4 A idle and under 40 A at full load on a stock pump (honda-tech 'EHPS Redone' write-up; diyelectriccar MR2 EHPS wiki), 70-80 A at maximum load on raised-pressure pumps (Alaria Tech FAQ); factory MR-S EHPS fuse 50 A (2002 MR2 EWD element list). Bussmann AMI time-current (Cooper Bussmann AMI series data sheet): 100% >= 100 h, 110% >= 4 h, 150% 90-3600 s, 200% 5-100 s - an 80 A peak is 133% of 60 A, so it holds well over 90 s, longer than any full-lock burst. Wire: 8 AWG 150 C single wire in free air 76 A (Thermal Wire and Cable ampacity table, AS50881 method) >= 60 A, so the fuse protects the wire; 10 AWG (55 A) would not. HCR150 relay moved from the engine bay to the glove box 2026-09-28 (Daniel: every relay in the cabin); drawn on ST185-B-cabin because its trigger is ECU-B B12
